what: The first run with a trained model in a kernel slot: the few-free-variables surrogate for instratus_condensate (an MLP predicting the two stratus fractions, the two in-stratus mixing ratios and two gates, the rest of the kernel's outputs derived by the routine's own closure) installed through --kernel-model in the cloud stage, 50 steps, replay boundary.
outcome: model run exited 255 at step 0 on all 512 ranks: PythonProcessContractError 'Python process payload differs across MPI ranks' from the cloud stage's install; no history, no summary
bfb_record_note: pi_cam_pausable_instratus-surrogate_vs_oracle_50step_bfb.json and the .health.json (512 tracebacks, no physics counts) were written by the job's comparison of an empty run and are not evidence of anything; the resubmitted run reuses the tag and overwrites both.
diagnosis: Not the physics and not the frame contract: the model's module kept its log-scaled feature names in a Python set.  Every rank loads the cloudpickled model and re-pickles it into the process payload, and a set of strings pickles in per-process hash order (PYTHONHASHSEED is randomised per process), so the 512 payloads hashed 512 ways and the install refused them.  Reproduced on the login node: two hash seeds give two different pickle hashes of the same model, one seed gives one.
disposition: The set became a tuple and the model was re-exported from the same trained weights (bit-identical outputs on 30 captured frames; one pickle hash under three hash seeds); the gate job fixes PYTHONHASHSEED while models are loaded; the payload-mismatch error now says why it happens.  Resubmitted under the same tag.
